title.en: Recognise keywords and write valid identifiers

say.en: Type print("Hello, Karnataka") and press Enter. Python answers at once. Why is Python so popular for beginners and experts alike? In this lesson: State the features of Python.
Use interactive and script mode.
Recognise keywords and write valid identifiers.

body.en: Python is a high-level, free and open-source language. It is interpreted, so statements are executed one by one. It is case-sensitive (Marks and marks are different names), portable across operating systems, and uses indentation to group statements. Python has two *modes*. In interactive mode we type a statement at the >>> prompt and see the result immediately. In script mode we save a program in a file with the .py extension and run the whole file.

title.en: On the board: Two ways to run Python, and naming rules

say.en: In interactive mode we type one statement at the prompt and see the result at once.
In script mode we save many statements in a .py file and run the whole file. It can be saved and run again.
Python is an interpreter: it runs one statement at a time, top to bottom.
An identifier may use letters, digits and underscore, must not start with a digit, and must not be a keyword.
Remember that Marks and marks are two different names, because Python is case-sensitive.

body.en: *Keywords* are reserved words with a special meaning, such as if, else, for, while, True, False, None, and, or, not, def and import; they cannot be used as names. Identifiers are names we give to variables and functions. Rules: an identifier may contain letters, digits and the underscore; it must not start with a digit; it cannot be a keyword; and it cannot contain spaces or special symbols like !, @, # or $.

heading.en: Python Basics: Features, Modes, Tokens and Variables

tagline.en: Why Python, interactive and script mode, the five kinds of tokens, rules for identifiers, variables and comments.

myth.en: Python does not care about capital letters, so Print("Hi") works like print("Hi").

truth.en: Python is case-sensitive. Print is an unknown name, so the program stops with NameError: name 'Print' is not defined. Some other software (like many search boxes) ignores case, so learners expect the same. In Python every identifier and keyword must match its exact spelling and case.

say.en: Python: high-level, interpreted, free and open source, case-sensitive, portable, uses indentation; by Guido van Rossum, 1991.
Interactive mode (>>> prompt, not saved) and script mode (.py file, saved, run with F5).
Five tokens: keywords, identifiers, literals, operators, punctuators.
Identifiers: letters, digits, _; not starting with a digit; no spaces or symbols; not a keyword.
A variable is created by assignment; # starts a comment.

takeaway.en: Python: high-level, interpreted, free and open source, case-sensitive, portable, uses indentation; by Guido van Rossum, 1991.

narration.en: Many people think: Python does not care about capital letters, so Print("Hi") works like print("Hi"). Actually: Python is case-sensitive. Print is an unknown name, so the program stops with NameError: name 'Print' is not defined. Some other software (like many search boxes) ignores case, so learners expect the same. In Python every identifier and keyword must match its exact spelling and case.

problem.en: Which of these are valid identifiers? total_marks, 2ndName, _count, for, roll no, Avg1

steps.en: total_marks, _count and Avg1 use only letters, digits and underscores and do not start with a digit: valid.
roll no contains a space: invalid.

answer.en: Valid: total_marks, _count, Avg1. Invalid: 2ndName, for, roll no.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. Which of these are valid identifiers? total_marks, 2ndName, _count, for, roll no, Avg1

say.en: Let us work through this together. Which of these are valid identifiers? total marks, 2ndName, _count, for, roll no, Avg1.
total marks, _count and Avg1 use only letters, digits and underscores and do not start with a digit: valid.
2ndName starts with a digit: invalid.
for is a keyword: invalid.
roll no contains a space: invalid.
So the answer is Valid: total marks, _count, Avg1. Invalid: 2ndName, for, roll no.
